newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes end firmer, sour crudes slip late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes end firmer, sour crudes slip late.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes ended Thursday stronger amid a shift in paper market buying away from heating oil to both crude and gasoline.

Cash crude players said the feature in the grade market was the late sell-off in sour barrels, which brought West Texas Sour/Midland down substantially against the West Texas Intermediate/Cushing marker.
The benchmark ended the session around 10-20 cents higher at $21.95-$22.05 a barrel, with the March/April WTI at about 25-27 cts.
Late deals saw Louisiana sweet barrels weaken in value.
